method: Same-agent English/Marathi block-by-block close reading, reverse reconstruction of the Henkin-language expansion and induction preserving consistency, direct replay of the strong-generalization contradiction and both saturated-instance equivalences, and exact formula, macro, token, tag, label, identifier and reference comparison after one documented source projection. No independent human or native-speaker review is claimed.
scope: Henkin expansion: new witness constants, saturated sentence sets, the consistency-preserving construction, and existential/universal instance membership.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Henkin's device adds denumerably many constants and a conditional for each one-free-variable formula so true existentials have witnesses, or false universals have counterexamples. Extending the language preserves consistency, and a saturated set contains one such conditional for every formula.
samples.checks: Both prvEx branches, free-variable condition, new-constant scope, language-expansion proposition and saturation biconditional are exact.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Enumerate all one-free-variable formulas in the enlarged language, choose each c_n fresh from its formula and all earlier D_i, and define D_n by the appropriate Henkin conditional. Add the D_n successively; the union is saturated, and an induction aims to show each finite stage remains consistent.
samples.checks: The A_i/x_i enumeration, freshness exclusions, D_n schemas, Gamma_n recursion, union, base case and induction-step assumptions preserve every index and set inclusion.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: If adding D_n caused inconsistency, Gamma_n would derive not-D_n and hence both the quantified antecedent and the negated or positive instance. Freshness permits strong generalization, producing a quantified contradiction already in Gamma_n, contrary to its consistency.
samples.checks: Every prvEx/prvAll branch, four-system strong-generalization reference, c_n freshness condition and final contradiction are preserved. OLCOM-001 restores only the missing x_n argument in one explanatory formula.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: A complete consistent saturated set contains an existential iff it contains one closed-term instance and contains a universal iff it contains every closed-term instance. Saturation supplies the difficult witness or counterexample directions; ordinary quantified derivability supplies the reverse directions.
samples.checks: Both tagged proposition items, closed-term quantifiers, saturation uses, inconsistency exercise, proof-system reference sets and membership conclusions remain exact.

source_observations: OLCOM-001 records the frozen explanatory formula forall-x-not-A_n with its x_n argument omitted; the Marathi target restores the argument fixed by all surrounding formulas.
The construction distinguishes the enlarged language L-prime, the finite stages Gamma_n and their saturated union Gamma-prime; those roles are retained throughout.
All remaining formulas, macros, controlled tokens, tags, labels, identifiers and reference options match exactly.
limitations: No independent human or native-speaker review has been performed.
हेंकिन विस्तार, संतृप्तता and the witness/counterexample pair remain expert-reviewable decisions T193, T190 and T194.
The exercises left implicit by the frozen source, including why inconsistency appears at a finite stage, are not supplied.
